newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union leader opposes SFP studio sale.
newsitem.headline: French union leader opposes SFP studio sale.

text.p: The head of the Communist CGT union, Louis Viannet, called on Wednesday for the government to drop the planned privatisation of the SFP film production studio.
"The government should renounce all ambitions to privatise SFP," he said in a statement, in which he said he would meet the staff on Thursday and encourage their opposition to the sale.

It was important to keep film production and distribution facilities in the public sector, given the growth of multimedia technologies and the development of digital and satellite television, he said.
He called for the purchase of the Societe Francaise de Production (SFP) by state-owned France Television, to protect taxpayers' interests and maintain quality of French programming.
Belgian production house LBO Convoi has emerged as a rival bider for SFP after French businessman Walter Butler put in a 50 million franc offer for the concern.

But Butler's bid has provoked labour anger as he would eliminate 667 out of a total 1,057 jobs if he won the bidding and received a requested 1.2 billion francs of state funds to cover the restructuring.
